title: Demak Sultanate
capsule: Demak was the first Islamic sultanate on Java, founded around 1475 on the north coast as a port dependency of the declining Hindu-Buddhist Majapahit empire, which it helped extinguish by c. 1527. Under its first sultan, Raden Patah, and his successor Trenggana (r. 1521–1546), Demak extended its authority across much of Java and sponsored the Islamization of the archipelago. Trenggana's death at the siege of Panarukan in 1546 triggered a succession crisis; by 1552 the sultanate fragmented, its territories passing to Pajang and later Mataram.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial boundaries are poorly attested; Demak's sphere of influence on Java is reconstructed from Javanese chronicle traditions (babad) and Portuguese accounts, with no contemporary cartographic evidence.
